answer: Each task commits to a domain-separated hash of its parameters and a future drand quicknet pulse; the challenge is derived only after threshold-BLS signatures fix that unpredictable pulse. An ember-like precomputed answer is hollow: offline sybil workers cannot know which instance to farm, and replayed work fails when the pulse changes. A ripple of fresh challenges makes parallel identities pay for verifiable work instead of reusing cached proofs.
